# Slice Tricks in Go

Go slices are highly versatile. There are several important techniques to master for efficient slice manipulation — from copying, deleting, inserting elements, to using three-index slicing.

## `copy(dst, src)` — Copying Slices

The `copy` function copies elements from `src` to `dst` and returns the number of elements copied. Copy does **not share memory** between slices.

```go
src := []int{1, 2, 3, 4, 5}
dst := make([]int, len(src))
n := copy(dst, src)
fmt.Println("Copied:", n)  // 5
fmt.Println("dst:", dst)   // [1 2 3 4 5]

// Modify dst — src unaffected
dst[0] = 99
fmt.Println("src:", src)   // [1 2 3 4 5]
fmt.Println("dst:", dst)   // [99 2 3 4 5]

// Partial copy — min(len(dst), len(src))
small := make([]int, 3)
copy(small, src)
fmt.Println("small:", small) // [1 2 3]
```

## Three-Index Slicing: `s[low:high:max]`

The three-index syntax limits the capacity of the new slice, preventing child slices from modifying elements beyond the intended bounds:

```go
arr := []int{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5}

// s[low:high:max] — max limits cap
s := arr[1:4:5]
fmt.Println(s)      // [1 2 3]
fmt.Println(len(s)) // 3
fmt.Println(cap(s)) // 4  (max-low = 5-1 = 4)

// Without max, cap extends to end of array
s2 := arr[1:4]
fmt.Println(cap(s2)) // 5  (len(arr)-low = 6-1 = 5)
```

## Deleting an Element — Append Trick

Go has no built-in delete function. The trick uses `append`:

```go
s := []int{1, 2, 3, 4, 5}

// Delete element at index i=2
i := 2
s = append(s[:i], s[i+1:]...)
fmt.Println(s) // [1 2 4 5]

// Delete first element
s2 := []int{10, 20, 30, 40}
s2 = s2[1:]
fmt.Println(s2) // [20 30 40]

// Delete last element
s3 := []int{10, 20, 30, 40}
s3 = s3[:len(s3)-1]
fmt.Println(s3) // [10 20 30]
```

## Inserting an Element

```go
func insertAt(s []int, i, val int) []int {
    s = append(s, 0)       // grow slice by one
    copy(s[i+1:], s[i:])  // shift elements right
    s[i] = val             // place value
    return s
}

nums := []int{1, 2, 4, 5}
nums = insertAt(nums, 2, 3)
fmt.Println(nums) // [1 2 3 4 5]
```

## Reversing a Slice

```go
func reverse(s []int) {
    for i, j := 0, len(s)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
        s[i], s[j] = s[j], s[i]
    }
}

nums := []int{1, 2, 3, 4, 5}
reverse(nums)
fmt.Println(nums) // [5 4 3 2 1]
```
